doc.title: Ruth Brown interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995

title: Freddie Green and the spirit of cooperation on the road
summary: Freddie Green is named the secret of the Basie band, and Brown recalls there was no competitiveness among the touring bands.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well you know other artists have come in here and we’ve talked about the Basie band and they’ve said those exact words.
Like they read it off a script.
Of course. It’s there. And he set beside Basie over 40 years. When Basie passed, he didn’t live long after that.

Freddie Green, that was his life. I saw him, he said, “Well Basie’s gone I don’t know what I’m gonna do.” And sure enough. But he sat there for over 40 years playing that [scats] that was the Basie band, you see? The simpler, the better. The simpler, the better. And of course Basie, he was such a wonderful individual. You know and I think the thing about those days that was really great was there was no competitiveness. Whatever was

good for the show, that’s what we did. We toured together, we rode the buses together, we lived under the same circumstances, we ate under the same circumstances, and when you went to the stage at night, it was a combined effort, you know? It wasn’t about who can outdo the other. It’s like here, we’re here as a unit, let’s make those people who bought the tickets glad they came, and let’s have them ask when we will be back again, you know. I think that was the thing that I remember most about it, you know. And I worked with Basie many, many times.
